security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, CSS grid examples, and expected .claude skill paths. The helper scripts are legitimate local tooling, but unvalidated paths and names can read or write outside intended project locations. No prompt injection, network access, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated HTML file path in extract-structure.sh
remediation.suggestion: Use realpath, reject absolute paths and .. segments, require .html files, and enforce containment in the approved prototype directory.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated module, template, and component names in scaffold-component.sh
remediation.suggestion: Validate names against safe identifier patterns, canonicalize output paths, and ensure generated files remain under frontend/src/modules.

remediation.issue: Generated structure files are written into a hidden skill directory
remediation.suggestion: Write generated reports to a project output folder or clearly document cleanup behavior for .claude skill artifacts.

static_findings.snippet: These are NOT valid DevPrep AI glassmorphism classes:

| `display-card` | Read-only content, stats | Card, Typography, badges |
| `layout-section` | Page sections, containers | Layout wrapper, grid/flex patterns |

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated HTML Path Can Traverse Project Boundaries
semantic_findings.description: extract-structure.sh accepts a caller-provided HTML path and concatenates it with PROJECT_ROOT before grep reads it. Without realpath containment or extension checks, ../ segments can read files outside the intended prototype folder.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code quotes variables, so command injection is unlikely. However, there is no path canonicalization or allowed-directory check before local reads.

semantic_findings.title: Scaffold Arguments Can Escape Intended Output Path
semantic_findings.description: scaffold-component.sh places --module and --name directly into output paths before writing a .tsx file. Values with path separators can write outside the expected components directory if the derived path exists or can be created.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script uses user arguments in mkdir and output redirection without identifier validation. The overwrite prompt reduces accidental replacement but does not prevent new path-traversal writes.

content.user_title: Convert HTML Designs to React Components
content.value_statement: Converting polished HTML prototypes into consistent React components is slow and error prone. This skill guides extraction, component mapping, scaffolding, implementation, and validation for glassmorphism interfaces.
actual_capabilities: Extracts component names, glassmorphism classes, interactive elements, and layout patterns from HTML prototypes.
Guides component naming, module placement, and shadcn/ui mapping decisions.
Scaffolds React TypeScript components from interactive, display, or layout templates.
Preserves approved glassmorphism utility classes during conversion.
Validates file size, interface naming, any types, class validity, and import patterns.
Provides examples and references for common component layouts.
limitations: Designed for React, TypeScript, shadcn/ui, and existing glassmorphism classes.
Generated components still need human business logic and state handling.
Shell scripts expect a specific project layout and existing target modules.
Path and component names should be reviewed before running scripts.

use_cases.title: Convert a finalized prototype
use_cases.description: Turn a completed HTML glassmorphism mockup into a typed React component with guided structure and validation.

use_cases.title: Standardize design system output
use_cases.description: Map repeated prototype patterns to shared shadcn/ui components and approved glassmorphism classes.

use_cases.title: Validate component quality
use_cases.description: Check generated components for file size, interface naming, any types, class usage, and import patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Convert one prototype
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a single finalized design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the design-to-production skill to convert .superdesign/design_iterations/glassmorphism_hints_panel_1.html into a React component. Ask me for module placement before scaffolding.

prompt_templates.title: Map components first
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow with review before file generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this HTML prototype and summarize the component name, target module, shadcn/ui mappings, glassmorphism classes, and recommended template before writing files.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold and validate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for an existing module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scaffold the approved component in the practice module, preserve valid glassmorphism classes, fill the template TODOs, and run the validation script afterward.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a complex section
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the hero section prototype into a layout-section component. Identify reusable child components, confirm responsive grid behavior, and report validation results.

output_examples.input: A designer provides a finished glassmorphism hints panel prototype.
output: Structure summary with detected buttons, classes, and layout pattern.
Recommended component name, module placement, and template type.

output_examples.input: A team needs a feature grid converted into a reusable React section.
output: Mapping from prototype elements to shared UI components.
Responsive layout guidance for mobile and desktop grids.
Quality report covering file size, imports, and class validity.

output_examples.input: A generated component fails the style validation step.
output: Clear list of failed checks and warnings.
Suggested replacements for invalid glassmorphism classes.
Next actions before the component is ready for review.

best_practices: Use finalized HTML prototypes and confirm the target module before scaffolding.
Review extracted classes and replace invalid glassmorphism utilities before implementation.
Run validation after filling TODOs and before committing the component.
anti_patterns: Do not run the scripts on untrusted file paths or names without review.
Do not use this skill for non React projects or unrelated visual styles.
Do not accept generated TODOs as complete business logic.

faq.question: Does this skill write production code automatically?
faq.answer: It scaffolds a React component and TODO structure. A developer still implements business logic and reviews output.

faq.question: What input does it need?
faq.answer: It needs a finalized HTML prototype path and an existing target module.

faq.question: Which UI stack does it support?
faq.answer: It targets React, TypeScript, shadcn/ui, and DevPrep AI glassmorphism classes.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it validate security?
faq.answer: No. It validates style and component quality only. Review script inputs before running local commands.

faq.question: Can I customize templates?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes template files for interactive cards, display cards, and layout sections.
